title: Drywall

sourceNotes: Preserve the user-selected parent line exactly; it is a development line, not represented as source quotation.
imagePrompt: Create one 1536 x 1024 pixel painted scene sheet, EXACTLY TWO COLUMNS BY THREE ROWS, six equal-width WIDE cinematic panels in row-major order 0 to 5. Each column is 768 pixels; rows are approximately 341, 341 and 342 pixels high. Hard straight cell edges; no gutters, no panel labels, no numbers, no captions, no typography, no readable lettering, no logos. Every cell is its own complete environment, never a sprite or a cutout. Use the polished watercolor and fine ink on textured cream paper style of Enough: warm directional light, deep teal and umber shadows, restrained paper grain, expressive natural faces, subtle imperfect painted edges. Human anatomy is believable, heads naturally sized; shoulders, elbows, wrists, hands, hips and knees belong to one continuous body. Seat hips on the actual seat, feet on the same floor, fingers visibly holding their actual objects; no disembodied hands, duplicated limbs, floating props or pasted-on heads. Keep important faces, hands, contact points and grounded figures within each wide panel with safe margins. Maintain the same identities, clothing, figure scale, prop design and spatial continuity across all six scenes. Anonymous original visual casting only, not likenesses of credited storytellers. This is a dramatic storyboard adaptation, not a claim that imagined symbols or staged details are verified events. Story: Drywall. Palette accents: #F6E6CB, #527E83, #DB7453. Identity continuity: TEEN: The same teenage boy throughout, warm medium tan skin, short dark brown hair, rust-orange shirt, slate trousers and plain shoes; a smaller adolescent body than the parent, never a tiny adult pasted onto the room. PARENT: The same adult mother throughout, deeper warm brown skin, long dark brown hair, muted teal blouse and slate skirt; calm face and naturally adult proportions. She is absent from the first two scenes, arrives through the doorway, then lowers herself rather than shrinking. TOP LEFT (frame 0): A narrow modest bedroom in late afternoon. The teen stands in three-quarter profile left of an intact plaster wall, one fist held tensely near his chest and the other hand down, shoulders raised, jaw tight. Both feet visibly bear weight on floorboards; a bed edge, closed door and small cleaning bucket establish the room without crowding the wall. Leave clear negative space between fist and plaster. His anger is private, not heroic violence. TOP RIGHT (frame 1): The same boy has just withdrawn his fist from a small fresh jagged hole in the same wall. His elbow bends naturally back toward his ribs, open fingers carry a little chalk dust, and his shocked face looks from his hand to the damage. Small plaster crumbs lie directly below the hole. The bucket and brush remain within reach but untouched. Keep the hole small and mundane, with no injury, explosion or glorified impact pose. MIDDLE LEFT (frame 2): The parent has entered the bedroom and stopped a respectful step from the teen. He stands beside the damaged wall, one arm relaxed and the other pointing directly at the actual hole, eyes lifting from the floor to her face. She listens with hands low and a concerned, unspectacular expression. Full joined arms and naturally sized hands; shared floor and doorway establish their real distance. The untouched bucket makes the admission a choice rather than an accomplished cover-up. MIDDLE RIGHT (frame 3): The parent lowers onto one knee beside the teen so their eyes meet naturally; her knee contacts the floor and her skirt folds around a believable leg. One hand rests on her own thigh and the other opens gently toward him, never wagging. His shoulders loosen while his face remains ashamed. The jagged hole stays visible just behind their shoulders, clear of both bodies. Warm light falls on the two faces; tenderness does not erase the consequence. BOTTOM LEFT (frame 4): The teen kneels on the bedroom floor and gathers plaster crumbs with a small brush into a dustpan. His fingers wrap the brush handle, the bristles meet the floor, and his forward knee supports the reach. The parent stays beside him at a modest distance, watching rather than taking over. The damaged wall is still conspicuous and unpatched. The teen's face is sober and determined; ordinary cleanup is the meaningful action. BOTTOM RIGHT (frame 5): The parent and teen share a gentle side embrace after cleanup, bodies balanced and feet or knees grounded; her forearm wraps naturally around his upper back and his near shoulder leans into her. Their faces soften without a giant grin. Set the brush and dustpan down visibly at their feet. Keep the unrepaired hole in unobstructed wall space beside them. The same narrow room now feels breathable, with responsibility and connection present together. Story-specific safeguards: The exact parent caption remains: You’re in trouble for what you did, but you’re out of trouble for being honest. This development line is not a verified source quotation. Do not display it as painted lettering. Do not show the parent present before their entrance or hide/repair the damage in the ending.
